recipes.name: Uncooked Banana Pudding
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed
1 (5 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Stir milk, sour cream, whipped topping, and pudding mix together in a bowl until well combined.
Place a layer of cookies in the bottom of a trifle bowl; cover with a layer of pudding mixture, then a layer of bananas. Repeat until all ingredients are used.

raw_recipe.headline: Uncooked Banana Pudding
raw_recipe.description: Quick and easy banana pudding with sour cream, milk, pudding mix, bananas, and whipped topping. No standing over a hot stove, just stir, layer, and serve.

review.reviewBody: This was excellent! I made it exactly as written except I soaked the sliced bananas in acidulated water to prevent them from turning brown. I sprinkled crushed vanilla wafters on the top because the picture with the whole cookies on top doesn't look very appealing. My husband, who loves banana anything, ate it all gone!

This is delicious and super-easy. I have made 2 double batches in the past week for people at my school, it went like hotcakes. Several people asked for the recipe. I used french vanilla pudding mix, one extra-creamy CoolWhip and one Vanilla CoolWhip, 8 oz. regular sour cream and 8 oz. light sour cream. I used about 1/2 cup less milk than the full quart needed so the pudding would not be soupy. I also used Pepperidge Farm Mini-Chessmen cookies in place of the vanilla wafers. I highly recommend using Chessmen cookies, either regular size or minis, anytime you make banana pudding. They really class up the taste. That said, if you are only making a single batch, I would use the regular sour cream instead of the light, since light sour cream has a much softer texture and probably would make a 'soupier' pudding. All in all, a wonderful pudding recipe and really quick and easy! Thanks for the posting!

I cut milk to 1 1/2 cups. Frozen whipped topping to measured 1 cup. Sour cream measured 1 cup. Mix vanilla pudding & milk thoroughly for 2 minutes then add sour cream, whipped topping and cut banannas thoroughly until all ingredients are one color. Note, banannas are still solid. Place 24 vanilla wafers in mix. Get wafers to be mixed well into the pudding. Then have pyrex deep casserole dish with wafers lining the bottom ready. Pour the wafer, bananna blended pudding into pyrex dish. Refrigerate 3 to 4 hours. A very close recipe is on a grocery chain store's brand box of vanilla wafers. These minor changes creates a more congealed pudding consistency.

This turned out fabulous! I used 8 oz of Fage 2% Greek yougert in place of the sour cream and sugar free vanilla pudding. I also used Pepperidge Farm Chessmen cookies that someone suggested. I put it in a 8x8 square pyrex dish and sprinkled chopped walnuts on top. Everyone loved it!

Oh my goodness! After reading the reviews & knowing I hate runny pudding I used a 5oz vanilla pudding & a 3.5oz cheese cake - made whipped topping then used 3c of that - mixed everything on,y using 1c milk - whipped that then waited 5 min for it to thicken - it was too thick so I added 1/2c more of the milk - I love this!! It's not too sweet it's just perfect the sour cream made this!!!!!! Thank you for sharing

I have been using this recipe for YEARS now and everyone loves it I always have to make a lot. I just usually go with it by taste. If you are making a lot buy 4 containers of cool whip, use almost the whole 16 oz of sour cream, use a splatter (not a lot) of vanilla extract, use one and a half of French vanilla instant pudding mix, only use a half cup of milk, Use 5 bananas, only use 3 bags of Pepperidge Farm Chessman cookies because the taste is better. Start off with putting your cookies at the bottom. And just start layering cookies, pudding, bananas, and repeat. When you are done, crumble some cookies for the top. And then you are done. I hope this helps.

Very tasty! Make your own whipped cream to sub for the tub and gently fold half of it in and put the rest on top! Also, sprinkle small chocolate truffle pieces on top. Who doesn’t love chocolate and banana’s?!?
I used a little less sour cream simply because I didn't have enough, and substituted with homemade whipped cream (heavy whipping cream, powdered sugar, and maple syrup)

This is a crowd pleaser, rich and delicious. I do substitute whipped heavy cream for Cool Whip and cream cheese for the sour cream. I do whip the cream cheese and add the condensed milk and beat them together.

This is my go-to recipe for banana pudding. My family loves it, and I always get rave reviews when I take it for potlucks. The only changes I make are to use French vanilla instant pudding for a richer flavor, and then I top it with another 8 oz. container of Cool Whip and crush the remaining vanilla wafers in the box to garnish on the top.

Everyone loved it! One even said, "Hate to say it, but this is better than my Grandma's!". A few small changes;(2)3.4oz boxes of pudding instead of (1)5.1oz box. For a thicker pudding I used 1½Cups of milk instead of 2. Also used 5 bananas instead of 4. On top of each layer of bananas I lightly sprinkled cinnamon sugar.
Everyone loves, 1/2 the sour cream
I love this, and I may be alone here, but I prefer using banana cream instead of vanilla pudding. Plan on making it half and half next time.
